LADAL hosts and participates in workshops, webinars, panels, and collaborative events that bring together researchers, students, and practitioners from around the world. **All events are free and open to the research community.**

## Upcoming Events {#upcoming}

We announce new workshops and webinars regularly. To be notified as soon as new events are scheduled, subscribe to the LADAL mailing list by emailing [ladal@uq.edu.au](mailto:ladal@uq.edu.au) with the subject line **email list**. Check back here for updates.

LADAL is also part of the [**Language Data Commons of Australia (LDaCA)**](https://ldaca.edu.au/) — visit the [LDaCA events page](https://ldaca.edu.au/events/) for additional opportunities.

---

## Past Workshops {#workshops}

LADAL offers practical, hands-on workshops on text analytics, statistics, data visualisation, and computational methods — from introductory sessions for beginners to advanced techniques for experienced researchers.

```{=html}
<div class="year-header">
  <span class="year-pill">2024</span>
  <div class="year-rule"></div>
</div>

<div class="workshop-list">

  <div class="workshop-card">
    <div class="workshop-header">
      <span class="workshop-date-badge">May 23–24, 2024</span>
      <div class="workshop-meta">
        <h4>Introduction to Computational Text Analytics</h4>
        <p class="ws-context"><a href="https://hass.uq.edu.au/Digital-Cultures-and-Societies/Research-Training">UQ Digital Cultures and Societies Hub</a> · 2 days</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="workshop-body">
      <p>An introduction to computational text analysis fundamentals using LADAL resources — suitable for researchers who have more text than they can analyse manually and want systematic, reproducible approaches.</p>
      <ul>
        <li>Why and where computational methods are appropriate</li>
        <li>Preparation and preconditions for computational text analysis</li>
        <li>R programming with Jupyter notebooks</li>
        <li>Common methods and libraries for text analysis</li>
        <li>Project management for computational research</li>
      </ul>
      <p><em>No programming experience required.</em></p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="workshop-card aqua">
    <div class="workshop-header">
      <span class="workshop-date-badge aqua">Feb 9, 2024</span>
      <div class="workshop-meta">
        <h4>Text Analytics for Humour Studies</h4>
        <p class="ws-context"><a href="https://ahsnhumourstudies.org/">Australian Humour Network 2024 Conference</a> · Half-day</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="workshop-body">
      <p>Showcasing how LADAL resources can elevate humour studies through computational methods. Covered text analytics techniques, data processing for humorous texts, visualisation of humour patterns, and practical applications.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

</div>
```

## Panels {#panels}

### Computational Thinking in the Humanities

```{=html}
<div class="panel-card">
  <div class="panel-card-header">
    <h3>Computational Thinking in the Humanities</h3>
    <div class="panel-meta">Thursday, 1 September 2022 · Online · 3 hours · 5–8 PM QLD | 10 AM–1 PM Finland | 8–11 AM UK</div>
    <div class="panel-partners">
      <span class="panel-partner-tag">ATAP</span>
      <span class="panel-partner-tag">FIN-CLARIAH</span>
      <span class="panel-partner-tag">Australian Digital Observatory</span>
      <span class="panel-partner-tag">UQ Digital Cultures Hub</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="panel-card-body">
    <p>An international workshop bringing together speakers from multiple countries to address fundamental questions: How can humanities embrace computing on their own terms? How do we resist having our problems "solved" for us? What are the methodological foundations of computational humanities? Does computation change the nature of what we do?</p>
    <p><strong>Part I — Plenary Talks</strong></p>
    <ul class="talks-list">
      <li>
```
